name: Clearyvo Media Cleanup
author: kishollo001

sections.description:
Scans the uploads folder in small resumable steps (no PHP time-limit problems) and classifies every image file:

  • Media Library originals, registered sizes, pre-scaling originals and image-editor backups: never moved.
  • Orphan sizes: name-300x200.jpg files whose original is in the Media Library but which WordPress no longer lists.
  • Files in backup / old / archive folders.
  • Plugin-managed folders and WebP/AVIF siblings: never touched.
  • Unregistered files.

Within every group of same-picture files the plugin keeps (1) the best copy in use (referenced, then registered) and (2) the highest-resolution copy. Other copies are only offered when they are unregistered, unreferenced, not recent, and verified:

  • Identical copies: same SHA-256.
  • Verified look-alikes: same picture at a lower or equal resolution, confirmed by a two-stage content comparison (16×16 prefilter, then a strict 32×32 neighbour-tolerant comparison). During the scan, Media Library images are read from a proportional registered size; right before a file is moved, the strict comparison is repeated on the real files. Anything that does not pass is listed as “unverified” and cannot be quarantined.

References are looked up in posts, post meta, term meta, user meta, settings (options), the active theme’s files and CSS files in uploads. Attachment-level use (featured image, wp-image-ID classes, block and gallery IDs, site icon, logo) is detected as well. Revisions and transients are ignored.

Heavy and oversized images (free): images the site serves that are heavier than 300 KB, larger than 2560 px on their longest side, or PNG files above 500 KB (usually photos in the wrong format), with where they are used.

“Delete” means quarantine: files move to a private folder and can be restored for the retention period (3, 7, 10 or 30 days; default 30), then they are removed automatically. Before every move the file is re-checked against the live site (unchanged, not newly referenced, not registered, kept copy still valid and identical in content). A “check only” pass runs first and shows what would happen.

Part of the Clearyvo plugin family: focused plugins that each check one part of your site and share one “Site Toolkit” menu with a Site health score. The Site Toolkit plugin has every checker in one plugin, switched on one by one; when it is installed, this plugin’s settings and results are shared with it. More at wp-sitechecker.com.

Free and Pro

  • Free: the full scan, exact copies, old resized versions, verified look-alikes, backup folders, full-size originals, heavy and oversized images (above 300 KB, larger than 2560 px, PNG photos), size statistics, selecting files by hand and the restorable quarantine.
  • Clearyvo Pro adds: image previews and picture families, the KEEP suggestion with its reason, everything proposed ticked at once and bulk removal, WebP and AVIF copies served at the same address, JPEG/PNG compression with verified backups, automatic optimisation of new uploads and of the library in the background, and optimisation reports with CSV export.

Clearyvo Pro is a separate add-on: the Pro features are its own code, not part of this plugin. One add-on adds the Pro features of every checker; it works with this plugin and with the Site Toolkit plugin.

Faster pages: WebP and AVIF copies (Clearyvo Pro)

For every JPEG/PNG the site serves (Media Library images and their sizes, and files found in use) a WebP copy is written next to it (photo.png -> photo.png.webp) and, where the server can write AVIF (WordPress 6.5+ with AVIF support in GD or Imagick), an AVIF copy (photo.png.avif). A copy is kept only when it is at least 10% smaller. Rules in wp-content/uploads/.htaccess give browsers the smallest format they accept (AVIF first, then WebP), at the same address, so posts, pages, page builders and the Media Library are not changed. Browsers that do not accept WebP get the original. The admin page checks from your browser whether the server really sends WebP.

  • Needs Apache or LiteSpeed (they read .htaccess). Nginx ignores .htaccess: the check then says so, and nothing changes for visitors.
  • When an image is replaced, regenerated or deleted, its copy is removed so an outdated picture is never shown. A scan also removes outdated copies.
  • “Remove all WebP and AVIF copies” deletes exactly the copies this plugin made (files from other tools are never touched) and removes the rules.
  • Deactivating the plugin stops serving the copies; reactivating serves them again after removing outdated ones. Deleting the plugin removes the copies and the rule.

JPEG/PNG compression (Clearyvo Pro)

Re-encodes JPEG (quality 60-95, default 82, progressive) and PNG (lossless) files the site serves. A file is replaced only if the new one is at least 5% smaller, opens, has the same pixel size (PNG: a spread of pixels, including transparency, is compared with the original). Before replacing, the original is copied to a protected folder inside the quarantine folder and verified; it stays for the quarantine retention (3, 7, 10 or 30 days). “Undo all compression” puts every original back, and refuses to overwrite a file that was changed after compression.

Left alone, with the reason in the report: JPEGs rotated through EXIF orientation, JPEGs with a colour profile other than sRGB, CMYK JPEGs, PNGs that are palette, grayscale, 16-bit, animated or carry a colour profile, files under 10 KB, files that do not fit the PHP memory limit. EXIF metadata is not kept in compressed JPEGs. The WordPress file size in the attachment data is updated.

  • Automatic optimisation: new uploads are queued and processed a few seconds after the upload by WP-Cron, so uploading is not slowed down.
  • Background optimisation: the files of the last scan are processed every 5 minutes (WP-Cron; a host cron job calling wp-cron.php makes it regular).
  • Reports: totals, before/after per type, every run, why files were left alone, problems, and a CSV of all files.
  • Deleting or replacing an image removes its record and backup; WebP copies of a compressed image are dropped and made again.

Full-size originals

When a photo larger than 2560 px is uploaded, WordPress keeps the original next to its “-scaled” copy and uses the copy everywhere. Unused originals can be moved to the quarantine; WordPress then treats the scaled copy as the original (original_image is removed from the attachment data). Restoring the file from the quarantine also puts that link back.

Limitations

  • Registered Media Library images are never moved. Registered duplicates are only listed (“merge manually”): this plugin does not rewrite content.
  • References built dynamically by plugin or template code cannot be seen. Plugin folders and plugin-generated images are therefore left alone, and every move goes to a restorable quarantine first.
  • Plugin files (other than the active theme and CSS in uploads) are not searched for references.
  • The reference check must be complete: if theme files could not be read, quarantine is disabled until a scan completes cleanly.
  • A scan older than 3 days must be repeated before quarantining.
  • Look-alikes are moved from their own list; each one is compared with the kept copy again, picture against picture, right before the move.
  • Needs PHP GD for visual comparison (exact duplicates and orphan sizes work without it) and a 64-bit PHP.
  • Per-site on multisite: the main site’s scan skips the sites/ folders of other sites.
  • The quarantine folder is inside wp-content (random name, protected with .htaccess/web.config). On Nginx add a deny rule for wp-content/wpmc-quarantine-*.

Filters

  • wpmc_backup_regex: regular expression that decides which folders count as backup folders.

Uninstall

Tables and settings are removed. Quarantined files are kept (together with the table that records where they belong) unless WPMC_REMOVE_QUARANTINE_ON_UNINSTALL is defined as true in wp-config.php.
sections.faq:
What is the /wp-json/clearyvo/v1/app/ address?

A read-only REST route for the Clearyvo Site Inspector Mac app. It shows the Site health score of the Clearyvo plugins to a signed-in administrator (for example with a WordPress Application Password) and changes nothing. It sends nothing anywhere: the app asks, the site answers.

Does it delete my images?

No. Files you choose are moved to a private quarantine folder, not deleted. You can put any of them back with one click for 3, 7, 10 or 30 days (you choose); only then are they removed for good. Before every move each file is checked again against the live site.

Which images can it remove?

Only files the site does not use: exact copies of a picture that stays, old resized versions WordPress no longer lists, verified smaller copies of the same picture, files in backup folders and, if you want, the full-size originals WordPress keeps next to its 2560 px copies. Images registered in the Media Library are never moved.

How does it know an image is used?

It looks for the file name, its URL and its Media Library ID in posts, pages, products, custom fields, term and user data, settings, the active theme’s files and CSS files in the uploads folder, including featured images, galleries, block IDs, the site icon and the logo. Image names that plugin code builds on the fly cannot be seen, which is why everything goes to a restorable quarantine first.

Will the scan slow down my site?

The scan runs in short steps while the page is open, so it finishes on shared hosting and on large libraries without timeouts. Visitors are not affected.

What if something is missing after a move?

Open the Quarantine list, tick the file and press Restore: it goes back to its original place (and, for full-size originals, back into the Media Library item).

What does Clearyvo Pro add?

Clearyvo Pro is a separate, paid add-on: image previews and picture families, a KEEP suggestion with its reason, everything proposed ticked at once and moving a whole list in one go, WebP and AVIF copies, JPEG/PNG compression with backups, automatic optimisation and reports. Everything listed under “Free” works without it.

Does it work with page builders and WooCommerce?

Yes. References in page builder data and product galleries are stored in posts and custom fields, which are searched. Plugin folders and images a plugin creates itself are left alone.

Does it work on multisite?

Per site: each site scans its own uploads folder. The main site’s scan skips the folders of the other sites.
sections.changelog:
1.21.5

  • Shared Clearyvo framework 2.3.1: the SEO checker is listed as Clearyvo SEO (formerly Image Alt & SEO) everywhere, whichever Clearyvo plugin loads the framework.

1.21.4

  • Database: every query goes through $wpdb->prepare(), with %i placeholders for table names.
  • Faster scan writes: batches of rows are saved in one transaction.

1.21.3

  • New icons: one design for the whole Clearyvo family, with a colour per group of checkers.

1.21.2

  • The other checkers in the shared menu have their new names (SSL Checker, Security Checker, Indexing Checker and the rest).

1.21.1

  • The plugin links point to wp-sitechecker.com again, until the site has moved to clearyvo.com.

1.21.0

  • New: read-only connection for the Clearyvo Site Inspector Mac app (Site health as data, for administrators with an Application Password).

1.20.1

  • Links to the new home of the Clearyvo WordPress plugins: clearyvo.com/wordpress.

1.20.0

  • First release under the Clearyvo name (folder and text domain: clearyvo-media-cleanup). Settings and results of the earlier versions are kept; activating this plugin switches the earlier copy off.
